comparator.name: Biomedical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught degree includes 120 EC of engineering and biomedical foundations, a 30 EC minor, and 30 EC of final-semester courses and project work.
components: Ethics 1: Philosophy of Science & Scientific Integrity
This 1 EC component is taken with the 4 EC Microbiology course.
Physics and Technology of Medical Imaging
Biomaterials specialization course in the first minor period.
Biomaterials specialization course in the second minor period.
The example takes Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine from the two final-semester choices.
Earn at least 145 EC in the degree, including all first-year courses and Safe Microbiological Techniques, and pass Research Course BME before starting the project.

routeSelection.basis: This example uses the first listed specialization, Biomaterials Science and Engineering, within the 30 EC deepening minor. It takes the two specialization courses, four minor electives and the tissue engineering elective in the final semester.

alternatives.label: Biomedical Science and Technology
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the selected courses and their applications.
alternatives.concept: Explore how biology, mathematics and computing can inform health technology. Study cells, anatomy and disease alongside signals, robotics, product design and image analysis.
progression: Cell biology and biochemistry precede laboratory work. Physiology and biochemistry precede pharmacology. Mathematics and programming precede signals, robotics and advanced data work.

alternatives.label: Health Technology Design and Innovation
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the selected courses and their applications.
alternatives.concept: Explore how health technology can be designed and introduced. Combine anatomy, physiology, public health and robotics with product design, market research, organizational psychology and business law.
progression: Biomedical and business foundations precede research, robotics and marketing. Public health, clinical context and technical study inform the final product-design course.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 6 courses and from the other focused plan by 12 courses in each direction.

alternatives.label: Biomedical Data and Image Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the selected courses and their applications.
alternatives.concept: Use mathematics and computing to analyze biomedical data and images. Study anatomy, physiology and neuroscience alongside signals, numerical models, databases and machine learning.
progression: Programming and introductory data science precede computer vision and machine learning. Mathematics precedes numerical methods, signal analysis and deep learning. Brain and behavior foundations precede advanced neuroscience.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 7 courses and from the other focused plan by 12 courses in each direction.

core: Biomedical life science, anatomy, physiology and disease
Mathematics, physics, mechanics and engineering systems
Programming, signals, medical imaging and computational modelling
Medical-device design, robotics, prosthetics and instrumentation
Biomaterials, implants, biofabrication and tissue engineering
Biomedical research, ethics and multidisciplinary collaboration
questions: How can engineering and computation improve diagnosis and therapy?
How can devices, prosthetics and artificial organs restore or monitor body functions?
How can healthcare technology support prevention, sustainability and responsible innovation?

candidates.label: Biomaterials & regenerative medicine
candidates.reason: UCR offers materials concepts, environmental materials processing and biological laboratory skills. These provide useful foundations, while a specialist plan requires sustained biomaterials characterization, fabrication and tissue engineering practice.

candidates.label: Health Technology Design and Innovation
candidates.assessment: Robotics and design methods, user research, health needs and organizational study support questions about introducing technology. The plan has limited scope in medical-device engineering, certification and hardware.

candidates.label: Biomedical Data and Image Analysis
candidates.assessment: Image processing, signals and computation support biomedical data analysis. Scanner physics, clinical protocols and specialist imaging laboratories remain distinct.

blocks: Groningen models transport in biological systems. UCR studies circulation and other body systems in Human Physiology.
Both study cell structure, signaling and division.
Both relate human anatomical structure to function. Groningen also includes physiology in this course.
Both study biomolecules and biochemical processes, including proteins and metabolism.
Both examine immune recognition and responses. UCR focuses on infection and host defenses.
Both use numerical methods for computational problems. UCR teaches Python separately.
Both use differentiation and integration for quantitative problems. UCR combines calculus with other mathematical methods.
Both use vectors, matrices and linear transformations.
Groningen studies the physics of medical imaging systems. UCR studies how to process images.
Both analyze signal and system behavior using transforms and frequency response.
Both develop probability and statistical inference for interpreting data.
Both develop image processing and analysis. UCR teaches general methods such as filtering and segmentation.
Groningen develops computation within the advanced biomedical engineering sequence.
Both develop concepts, specifications and prototypes. UCR works on general consumer products.
Groningen prepares students for biomedical engineering research. UCR offers general methods and statistics.
Groningen studies philosophy of science and research integrity. UCR studies broader ethical theories.
Groningen applies mechanics to biological structures and movement.
Groningen studies material properties for engineering applications.
Groningen develops experimental physics skills in the laboratory.
Groningen studies how materials interact with biological systems.
Both develop microbiology through bacterial work. The UCR lab also uses protein and DNA techniques.
Groningen credits safe microbiological techniques alongside its microbiology course.
Groningen studies the dynamics and vibration of mechanical systems.
Groningen teaches mathematical tools for biomedical engineering problems.
Groningen applies design methods to biomedical products. UCR offers general product design.
Groningen develops electricity and magnetism for engineering.
Groningen applies ethical reasoning to biomedical engineering.
Groningen teaches thermodynamics as a dedicated engineering subject.
Groningen studies waves and optics as a dedicated engineering subject.
Groningen offers a dedicated electronics course.
Groningen applies specialist biomaterials methods in the laboratory.
Groningen studies fabrication for biomedical applications.
Groningen develops biomedical measurement and instrumentation.
Groningen studies polymers for biomedical applications.
Groningen studies how to characterize material surfaces.
Groningen develops ethical reasoning for the research project.
Groningen studies tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
Groningen requires a supervised 15 EC research or design project. UCR shows optional independent research separately.

selection.assessment: A defensible closest UCR response combines biomedical science, computation, imaging, design and robotics while recording the missing physics and materials sequence. Medical-device innovation and medical imaging/data are separately evidenced, coherent, mechanically feasible and pairwise distinct. A biomaterials route was assessed but rejected as infeasible; production stops at the maximum of three included alternatives.

notes.text: Groningen combines engineering design with mechanics, electronics, materials science, specialist laboratories and a required project. The UCR options combine related biomedical study with data analysis, robotics, product design and innovation.

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught degree applies engineering to questions in health and medicine, including imaging, devices and biomaterials.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Groningen example uses the Biomaterials Science and Engineering minor. The UCR options emphasize biomedical science and technology, health technology design, or biomedical data and image analysis.
